The formulation is compatible with existing solvers. In simulation, the resulting safety filters nearly eliminate the collisions of certaintyequivalent HJ and are less conservative than equally safe uncertainty-padding baselines. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/HimanshuPaudel/Estimation-Aware-Reachability
tldr: This paper extends Hamilton-Jacobi reachability to account for robot belief, estimate, and uncertainty, treating unexpected measurements as an adversary to generate safety filters that outperform certainty-equivalent HJ and uncertainty-padding baselines in simulation.
tldr_zh: 本文将Hamilton-Jacobi可达性扩展到考虑机器人信念、估计和不确定性，将意外测量视为对手，生成的安全过滤器在模拟中优于确定性等价HJ和不确定性填充基线。
summary_zh: Hamilton-Jacobi可达性分析计算了系统在最坏情况扰动下能够保持安全的状态集合，但该方法假设状态是精确已知的，而实际机器人依赖于带有噪声的估计，其不确定性随运动演化。我们将Hamilton-Jacobi可达性扩展到机器人的信念、估计和不确定性上，将意外测量视为有界对手，并通过当前不确定性扩大不安全集合，从而使被认证的状态以指定概率保持安全。该公式与现有求解器兼容。在仿真中，所生成的安全滤波器几乎消除了确定性等价HJ方法中的碰撞，并且相比同等安全性的不确定性填充基线方法保守性更低。实现代码可在 https://github.com/HimanshuPaudel/Estimation-Aware-Reachability 获取。

title: RoboDx: Repair and Diagnosis of Faults in Robot Software
summary: A patch to a robot's navigation software can pass every unit test and still drive the robot off its path. Checking how the repaired robot drives catches such patches. It does not show that the agent found everything that was wrong. We introduce RoboDx, a generator of repair tasks for simulated robot navigation software with known injected faults. A hidden verifier marks a repair as verified only if the robot then drives correctly in hidden scenarios, which the agent never sees. A second track hides the code and asks the agent to pick the cause from a list of hypotheses. A task with two faults can contain a quiet fault, a fault that makes no hidden scenario fail unless the other fault is also present. On our set of 100 tasks, RoboDx-Hard-100, almost every repair by Claude Opus 5.5 with standard coding tools is verified. We analyse 94 of the tasks, 44 with one fault and 50 with two. On the 50 two-fault tasks, only 17 of Opus's 49 verified repairs remove both injected edits. Most faults left behind are configuration constants whose correct value the task's documentation does not state. Opus names both faults on 10/50 of these tasks when it cannot see the code. We then give four current models the same measurements of each faulty robot, picked so that, in the simulator, only the true cause produces all of them. The models name the cause on at most 38 of 94 tasks. They are right on almost all when they also get the simulator's output for every hypothesis. Their own predictions of that output give no detectable gain. On 97 tasks from real bug-fix pull requests, Claude Haiku 5.5, the weakest model on the generated tasks, scores lowest, and the other three models are not ordered.
tldr: RoboDx introduces a benchmark for diagnosing and repairing faults in simulated robot navigation software, revealing that language models often fail to identify all injected faults, especially configuration constants, and that current models perform poorly on hidden-cause diagnosis.
tldr_zh: RoboDx 提出了一个用于模拟机器人导航软件故障诊断与修复的基准，揭示了语言模型在识别所有注入故障（尤其是配置常量）方面的不足，并且当前模型在隐藏原因诊断上表现不佳。
summary_zh: 摘要：对机器人导航软件的一个补丁可能通过所有单元测试，却仍会导致机器人偏离路径。检查修复后的机器人实际行驶情况可以捕获此类补丁，但并不能证明代理已发现所有问题。我们提出RoboDx，一个为模拟机器人导航软件生成修复任务的系统，其中包含已知注入的故障。一个隐藏的验证器仅在机器人于隐藏场景中正确行驶时（这些场景代理从未见过）才将修复标记为已验证。另一条赛道隐藏代码，要求代理从假设列表中选择故障原因。一个包含两个故障的任务可能包含一个“静默故障”——即除非另一个故障同时存在，否则该故障不会导致任何隐藏场景失败。在我们的100个任务集RoboDx-Hard-100上，使用标准编码工具的Claude Opus 5.5几乎每一次修复都被验证。我们分析了其中94个任务，44个为单故障，50个为双故障。在50个双故障任务中，Opus的49个已验证修复中仅有17个同时移除了两处注入编辑。大多数遗留故障是配置常量，其正确值在任务文档中并未说明。当Opus无法看到代码时，它在10/50个此类任务中能同时指出两个故障。随后，我们为四个当前模型提供了每个故障机器人的相同测量数据，这些数据经过精心挑选，使得在模拟器中只有真正的原因能全部产生这些结果。模型在94个任务中最多在38个上正确指出原因。当它们同时获得每个假设的模拟器输出时，几乎在所有任务上都能答对。而它们自己对输出的预测并未带来可检测的提升。在来自真实修复缺陷拉取请求的97个任务上，Claude Haiku 5.5——在生成任务上表现最弱的模型——得分最低，而其他三个模型之间没有明显排序。

title: Measuring the Conservatism of Latent Safety Filters for World Models
summary: A latent safety filter decides from the latent of a world model whether a planned action is safe. Conformal calibration sets the threshold of the filter so that it accepts an unsafe action only with a small probability. However, the filter can still be conservative and refuse many safe actions, depending on the latent. To measure the conservatism that a latent forces on the filter, we group similar latents and actions into cells. A filter that gives one decision per cell can refuse the unsafe transitions of a cell only by refusing the safe ones in it as well. We call the share of safe transitions that lie in such cells the overlap. We prove that the overlap is the minimum share of safe transitions that such a filter has to refuse in order to accept no unsafe transition in the data. Both the overlap and the conformal calibration can be applied to any latent. We use this to compare three existing designs, in which the safety labels train a classifier on top of the world model, the world model itself, or a separate encoder beside it. In a visual navigation task, the separate encoder has the lowest overlap, and at the same conformal level its filter refuses the fewest safe actions and lets the planner reach the most goals of the three.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to measure the conservatism of latent safety filters in world models, proving that the overlap metric quantifies the minimum safe actions refused, and compares three filter designs in a visual navigation task.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种衡量世界模型中潜在安全滤波器保守性的方法，证明了重叠度量可量化拒绝安全动作的最小比例，并在视觉导航任务中比较了三种滤波器设计。
summary_zh: 摘要：潜在安全过滤器根据世界模型的潜在表示来判断计划动作是否安全。共形校准为该过滤器设定阈值，使其仅以较小概率接受不安全动作。然而，过滤器仍可能过于保守，并拒绝许多安全动作，具体取决于潜在表示。为衡量潜在表示对过滤器施加的保守程度，我们将相似的潜在表示与动作分组为单元。若过滤器为每个单元给出单一决策，则拒绝某个单元中的不安全转移只能以同时拒绝其中的安全转移为代价。我们将此类单元中安全转移所占比例称为重叠率。我们证明，为使过滤器在数据中不接受任何不安全转移，重叠率是其必须拒绝的安全转移的最小比例。重叠率与共形校准均可应用于任何潜在表示。我们据此比较了三种现有设计，其中安全标签分别用于在世界模型之上训练分类器、训练世界模型本身，或训练与之并列的独立编码器。在视觉导航任务中，独立编码器的重叠率最低，且在相同共形水平下，其过滤器拒绝的安全动作最少，使得规划器在三种设计中达成目标数量最多。

title: Neural Circuit Architectural Priors for Rat Locomotion
summary: Animals generate behavior through continuous interactions between their neural circuits, bodies, and environment. Embodied simulations study these interactions by testing neural circuit models in biologically realistic settings. Recent efforts have simulated diverse animals, and emerging work on biologically grounded neural architectures has begun to integrate circuit connectivity and single-unit dynamics from experimental data into artificial neural networks, introducing stronger inductive biases and closer mechanistic alignment with biology. How can we develop embodied simulations that enable the study of increasingly complex bodies and neural circuits? In this work, we address the challenge through coordinated advances in the simulated body, neural architecture, and training infrastructure. We introduce Rat v2, an efficient and flexible biomechanical body for simulating rat behavior. To control this body, we develop Rat NCAP, a biologically grounded neural architecture for locomotion based on mammalian spinal circuits that incorporates cell-type-specific connectivity and a novel flexor-extensor neuromechanical interface. To optimize circuit parameters, we develop GPU-accelerated simulation and training infrastructure. The model learns to locomote at different speeds and transition between gaits without imitation learning, producing locomotion statistics, kinematics, and cell-type-specific neural activity consistent with experimental data. Analyses reveal that the neuromechanical interface substantially affects trainability and gait quality, and in silico cell-type ablations reproduce known gait phenotypes and predict gait changes under graded perturbations. Together, these findings support the view that embodied simulations at an intermediate level of abstraction can simultaneously reproduce complex behavior and yield mechanistic insights into the neural circuits that generate it.
tldr: This paper presents Rat v2, a biomechanical rat body and Rat NCAP, a biologically grounded neural architecture based on spinal circuits, trained via GPU-accelerated simulation to produce realistic locomotion gaits and neural activity without imitation learning.
tldr_zh: 本文提出Rat v2生物力学大鼠模型和基于脊髓回路的生物神经架构Rat NCAP，通过GPU加速仿真训练，无需模仿学习即可产生真实步态和神经活动。
summary_zh: 动物通过其神经回路、身体与环境之间的持续交互产生行为。具身模拟通过在生物学真实环境中测试神经回路模型来研究这些交互。近期研究已对多种动物进行了模拟，而新兴的基于生物学的神经架构研究开始将实验数据中的回路连接性和单单元动力学整合到人工神经网络中，引入了更强的归纳偏置，并使机制与生物学更加对齐。我们如何发展能够支持对日益复杂的身体和神经回路进行研究的具身模拟？在本工作中，我们通过在模拟身体、神经架构和训练基础设施方面的协调推进来应对这一挑战。我们引入了Rat v2，一个高效且灵活的生物力学身体模型，用于模拟大鼠行为。为了控制该身体，我们开发了Rat NCAP，一种基于哺乳动物脊髓回路、融合了细胞类型特异性连接性和新型屈肌-伸肌神经力学接口的生物学基础神经架构。为了优化回路参数，我们开发了GPU加速的模拟与训练基础设施。该模型无需模仿学习即可学习以不同速度运动并在步态之间转换，产生的运动统计、运动学特征及细胞类型特异性神经活动均与实验数据一致。分析表明，神经力学接口显著影响可训练性和步态质量，而计算机内的细胞类型消融实验重现了已知的步态表型，并预测了分级扰动下的步态变化。综合来看，这些发现支持以下观点：在中等抽象层次上的具身模拟能够同时再现复杂行为，并为生成该行为的神经回路提供机制性洞见。

title: Feedback-Linearised Trajectory Tracking via Model-Informed Robust Geometric DDPC
summary: Data-driven predictive control (DDPC) predicts system responses from recorded trajectories, but nonlinear dynamics can limit the accuracy of fixed linear predictors. This paper studies geometric robust DDPC for trajectory tracking of a fully actuated manipulator using model-based feedback linearisation. A mechanical model maps virtual acceleration commands into joint torques, while recorded data capture residual dynamics arising from imperfect model parameters. The controller minimises worst-case prediction error over an open Grassmannian ball centred at the fitted trajectory subspace. Simulations on a planar 2R manipulator under gravity compare the proposed method with double-integrator model predictive control (MPC) and direct regularised data-enabled predictive control (DeePC). Results show improved tracking over double-integrator MPC despite increased torque effort, while performance relative to DeePC depends on the reference trajectory.
tldr: This paper presents a data-driven predictive control method for robotic manipulator trajectory tracking that uses model-based feedback linearization and geometric robust optimization over Grassmannian manifolds to handle nonlinear residual dynamics, demonstrating improved tracking over double-integrator MPC in simulations.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种基于模型反馈线性化与Grassmann流形鲁棒优化的数据驱动预测控制方法，用于机械臂轨迹跟踪，仿真表明其跟踪性能优于双积分器MPC。
summary_zh: 数据驱动预测控制（DDPC）根据记录轨迹预测系统响应，但非线性动力学可能限制固定线性预测器的精度。本文研究基于模型反馈线性化的全驱动机械臂轨迹跟踪几何鲁棒DDPC方法。机械模型将虚拟加速度指令映射为关节力矩，而记录数据捕获因模型参数不完善而产生的残余动态。控制器在拟合轨迹子空间为中心的开格拉斯曼流形球上最小化最坏情况预测误差。在重力作用下的平面2R机械臂仿真中，将所提方法与双积分器模型预测控制（MPC）和直接正则化数据使能预测控制（DeePC）进行比较。结果表明，尽管力矩消耗增加，所提方法相较于双积分器MPC在跟踪性能上有所提升，而与DeePC相比的性能则取决于参考轨迹。

title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition
summary:
Goal recognition is the task of inferring an agent's intended goal from its observed behavior. Most existing work focuses on high-level symbolic recognition, abstracting away the continuous motion through which agents reach their goal. Methods that do reason over continuous trajectories rely on an explicit dynamics model that is hard to acquire and rarely transfers across settings. Neither approach explicitly learns how agents move toward each candidate goal, limiting accuracy on ambiguous trajectory prefixes where such knowledge is most needed.
  We present WoRD (Waypoint Recognition with Diffusion), which uses a learned trajectory prior to infer the agent's goal from partial observations. At each step, WoRD runs one warm-started denoising chain per candidate goal, steers each chain toward the observed trajectory through a closed-form log-likelihood gradient, and reweights the resulting samples by Bayes' rule into a calibrated posterior over goals. We evaluate WoRD on simulated robot settings, pedestrian trajectories, and vehicle trajectories using four metrics targeting distinct failure modes. Across all three settings, the same inference procedure preserves calibrated multimodal beliefs through ambiguous prefixes where filter- and classifier-based observers collapse to a single mode or grow overconfident.
tldr: WoRD uses a learned trajectory prior with diffusion to infer an agent's goal from partial observations, producing calibrated posterior beliefs over goals in simulated robot, pedestrian, and vehicle settings.
tldr_zh: WoRD利用学习的轨迹先验和扩散模型，从部分观测中推断智能体的目标，并在模拟机器人、行人和车辆场景中生成校准的后验目标信念。
summary_zh:
目标识别是一项从智能体已观测行为中推断其预期目标的任务。现有研究大多聚焦于高层级的符号识别，忽略了智能体达成目标所依赖的连续运动过程。那些确实对连续轨迹进行推理的方法，则依赖于难以获取且难以在不同场景间迁移的显式动力学模型。这两种方法均未显式学习智能体如何朝每个候选目标运动，从而在轨迹前缀存在歧义时限制了识别精度——而恰恰在这些场景下，此类知识最为关键。

我们提出WoRD（基于扩散的航点识别），该方法利用学习得到的轨迹先验，从部分观测中推断智能体的目标。每一步中，WoRD针对每个候选目标运行一条热启动去噪链，通过闭式对数似然梯度将每条链引导至观测轨迹，并通过贝叶斯规则将所得样本重加权，形成校准的目标后验分布。我们在仿真机器人场景、行人轨迹和车辆轨迹上，使用四种针对不同失效模式的指标对WoRD进行评估。在上述三种场景中，相同的推理流程均能在歧义前缀阶段保持校准的多模态信念，而基于滤波器和基于分类器的观测方法在此类阶段会坍缩至单一模态或变得过度自信。

title: Capability Composition in Heterogeneous Teams via Barrier-Guided Diffusion Sampling
summary: The agents in a heterogeneous team can cooperate to accomplish tasks that exceed their individual capabilities. The team trajectories for a cooperative task can be generated by a generative model, provided that the model has been trained on demonstrations of the agents cooperating. Yet, demonstrations of cooperation are costly and may not exist for tasks that the team has never performed. The conditions under which the agents can combine their capabilities, however, are physical properties of the team and are known before any demonstration is collected. We encode the conditions as constraints on the team trajectories, and we enforce the constraints while sampling from generative models trained on demonstrations of each agent alone. We prove that the proposed method can generate every team trajectory that satisfies the constraints, although the demonstrations contain no cooperation. Hence the constraints determine which team trajectories can be generated, and the demonstrations determine how likely each team trajectory is. Numerical results on two cooperative tasks show the effectiveness of the method, which generates cooperative team trajectories that satisfy the constraints and requires no retraining when agents join or leave the team. Finally, we implement the method on a multi-robot testbed.
tldr: This paper proposes a barrier-guided diffusion sampling method to generate cooperative team trajectories for heterogeneous multi-robot teams without requiring demonstrations of cooperation, by encoding physical capability constraints and using individual agent demonstrations.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种基于障碍引导的扩散采样方法，通过编码物理能力约束并利用个体智能体的演示，在无需合作演示的情况下生成异构多机器人团队的合作轨迹。
summary_zh: 异构团队中的智能体可以通过协作来完成超出其个体能力的任务。针对协作任务的团队轨迹可以由生成模型生成，前提是该模型已基于智能体协作的演示数据完成训练。然而，协作演示数据成本高昂，且对于团队从未执行过的任务，此类数据可能并不存在。然而，智能体能够结合各自能力的条件是团队的物理属性，并且在收集任何演示数据之前便已知晓。我们将这些条件编码为对团队轨迹的约束，并在从基于各智能体单独演示训练得到的生成模型中进行采样时强制执行这些约束。我们证明，尽管演示数据中不包含协作行为，所提方法仍能生成所有满足约束的团队轨迹。因此，约束决定了哪些团队轨迹可以被生成，而演示数据则决定了每条团队轨迹的可能性大小。两个协作任务的数值结果表明了该方法的有效性，其能够生成满足约束的协作团队轨迹，并且在智能体加入或离开团队时无需重新训练。最后，我们在多机器人测试平台上实现了该方法。

title: Conceptual full-vehicle modeling of a modular all-wheel-drive robotic ADS test platform as a foundation for a digital twin architecture
summary: This paper presents the development of an initial full-vehicle simulation model of the PixKit modular electric test platform in IPG CarMaker. The objective is to create a physics-based and extendable model structure that can serve as a low-level foundation for future digital twin applications. The reference vehicle is a skateboard chassis combining unconventional vehicle characteristics such as four independent wheel-hub motors and rear axle steering capable of high steering angles. Since complete measurement data of the vehicle is not yet available, the model parameterization is based on a combination of manufacturer documentation, derived values and engineering assumptions. The modeling approach focuses on the system-level integration of the main vehicle subsystems rather than on a fully validated representation. The resulting model was assessed through basic driving scenarios with different steering inputs and configurations. The simulations showed stable model behavior and physically plausible interaction between the subsystems. The all-wheel-drive configuration produced symmetric wheel responses in longitudinal driving, while counter-phase rear axle steering increased the yaw response and reduced the simulated turning circle diameter compared with front axle steering only. The circular driving scenario further indicated bounded roll and slip behavior. Overall, the implemented CarMaker model provides a traceable and functional simulation basis for the PixKit vehicle. It can support future model refinement, calibration with real vehicle data and development with the goal of creating a validated digital twin architecture.
tldr: The paper presents a full-vehicle simulation model of the PixKit modular electric test platform in IPG CarMaker as a foundation for a digital twin, focusing on system-level integration and basic driving scenario validation.
tldr_zh: 本文介绍了在IPG CarMaker中构建PixKit模块化电动测试平台的整车仿真模型，作为数字孪生架构的基础，并进行了基本驾驶场景验证。

title: Hydrodynamics of robotic micro-swimmers in confinement
summary: Inspired by seminal work by E.M. Purcell, we discuss the problem of predicting and optimizing the performance of autonomous robots swimming in confinement. Our approach is based on the explicit numerical resolution of the fluid flow induced by the swimmer, and it is validated experimentally on a cm-size prototype composed of a cargo head and a rotating propulsive tail. Using hydrodynamic scaling, we predict the performance of replicas of our prototype scaled down to mm- and sub-mm-size to test the feasibility of autonomous micro-robots navigating in narrow vessels. The main result of our theoretical, computational, and experimental analysis is that, while hydrodynamics seems to place no fundamental obstruction to the vision of autonomous micro-robots navigating in narrow lumens inside the human body, it does provide useful and strict guidelines for rational design at different length scales.
tldr: The paper uses hydrodynamics simulations and a cm-scale robot prototype to analyze and predict the performance of autonomous micro-swimmers in confined environments, deriving design guidelines for future sub-mm-scale medical robots.
tldr_zh: 本文通过流体动力学模拟和厘米级机器人样机，分析并预测了受限环境中自主微型游泳机器人的性能，为未来亚毫米级医疗机器人提供了设计指导。

title: Facet-SLAM: Real-Time Triangle Splatting SLAM
summary: Dense SLAM systems based on 3D Gaussian splatting build maps that render photorealistically, but their surface geometry is poor, and obtaining a mesh requires extraction or fusion stages. Triangle splatting avoids this with surface primitives whose vertices can be triangulated directly into a connected mesh, yet SLAM with this representation has so far relied on photometric tracking, which is too slow for localization at sensor rate. We present Facet-SLAM, the first real-time triangle splatting SLAM system for RGB-D cameras. Fast geometric registration is the natural alternative, but it is not sufficient alone, since the mapper's optimization displaces triangles from the observed surface and makes them unreliable registration targets. We therefore separate the two roles: the tracker sets each triangle's centroid from fused depth and registers frames to these centroids by GICP, while the mapper is restricted to non-translating updates via a change of variables. Our system achieves competitive tracking accuracy at around 100 FPS on a desktop GPU and runs at sensor rate on a Jetson AGX Orin. Compared with the photometric approach, it is over 20 times faster, matches rendering quality, and improves surface accuracy, reducing the chamfer distance of the Delaunay mesh on Replica from 1.55 to 0.86 cm. We will release the implementation at https://github.com/edward62740/Facet-SLAM.
tldr: Facet-SLAM is the first real-time triangle splatting SLAM system for RGB-D cameras, using fast GICP-based geometric registration and a non-translating mapper to achieve competitive tracking accuracy at ~100 FPS and improved surface mesh quality.
tldr_zh: Facet-SLAM 是首个基于三角形溅射的实时 RGB-D SLAM 系统，通过快速 GICP 几何配准和限制平移的建图器，实现了约 100 FPS 的跟踪速度并提升了表面网格精度。

title: Scalable Iterative Multi-Agent Path Finding under Turn Constraints
summary: Large-scale multi-mobile-robot systems require fast and reliable path planning under realistic motion constraints. Multi-Agent Path Finding with turn actions (MAPF$_T$) explicitly models orientation changes and turn-induced delays, but these constraints increase the computational burden of search-based methods. Priority-inheritance-based planning offers a highly scalable alternative, yet directly extending it to MAPF$_T$ is nontrivial because turn actions break the immediate node-vacation assumption underlying conventional priority inheritance. To address this challenge, this paper proposes PIBT$^*_T$, an efficient iterative solver for MAPF$_T$. PIBT$^*_T$ advances scalable multi-agent coordination by preserving the lightweight single-timestep planning mechanism of Priority Inheritance with Backtracking (PIBT), while introducing dedicated mechanisms to handle turn-induced dependencies, local deadlocks, livelock, and inefficient repeated pushing. Experiments on standard MAPF benchmarks show that PIBT$^*_T$ achieves high success rates and strong scalability, solving instances with up to 1000 agents within seconds. For realistic engineering environments, Action Dependency Graph (ADG)-based execution simulation and a flexible manufacturing system case study show that turn-aware planning better reflects robot execution and reduces actual makespan compared with classical MAPF planning. Experiments with TurtleBot4 robots further validate the practical feasibility of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper introduces PIBT*_T, a scalable iterative multi-agent path finding algorithm that explicitly handles turn constraints, achieving high success rates on up to 1000 agents and validated with TurtleBot4 robots.
tldr_zh: 本文提出 PIBT*_T，一种可扩展的迭代式多智能体路径规划算法，显式处理转向约束，在多达1000个智能体上实现高成功率，并通过TurtleBot4机器人验证。

title: Control-Aware Separating Hyperplanes for Control Barrier Functions in Planar Navigation
summary: Separating hyperplanes are widely used in Control Barrier Function (CBF)-based collision avoidance, yet their orientations strongly govern control intervention-the deviation of the applied control from the robot's nominal command. Existing methods typically select hyperplane orientations from geometry alone. Jointly optimizing orientations and control yields a continuous, non-convex problem in which local nonlinear solvers suffer from initialization sensitivity, local minima, and unpredictable latency, while discretized orientation grids scale exponentially with obstacle count. For planar navigation of a polygonal robot among polygonal obstacles, we present a solver-free, control-aware separating hyperplane selection method that directly computes a global optimum of this joint problem at each step whenever it is feasible. Exploiting the geometry of Minkowski difference polygons, we reduce this continuous non-convex optimization to evaluating a polynomial-size set of candidate control interventions via closed-form algebraic checks, selecting the feasible candidate of minimum norm. Across 250 simulated navigation scenarios, our method reduces cumulative intervention cost by 3.6% at the median and 27.3% at the 90th percentile compared to a local nonlinear solver, and completion time by 0.6% and 5.6%, respectively. In scalability benchmarks, it achieves a 6.1x per-step speedup at 16 simultaneous obstacles.
tldr: This paper presents a solver-free, control-aware method for selecting separating hyperplane orientations in CBF-based planar navigation, directly computing the global optimum of the joint orientation-control optimization by exploiting Minkowski difference polygon geometry.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种无求解器的控制感知分离超平面选择方法，用于平面导航中的CBF碰撞避免，通过利用闵可夫斯基差多边形几何直接计算方向-控制联合优化的全局最优解。

title: VESPA: Verifiable Symbolic Policy Adaptation for Safe Reinforcement Learning
summary: Safe reinforcement learning (RL) aims to prevent agents from taking actions that are dangerous or destructive to their environment. This is especially important for safety-critical domains, such as robotics or autonomous driving. Formal verification can be used to prove agent safety through safety constraints. However, in practice, many policies do violate safety constraints, and thus are verified to be unsafe. Since the goal is to obtain a safe policy, we would need to retrain a new policy from scratch and then verify it again until a candidate happens to pass. Both training and verification are usually not cheap, which makes this process inefficient. We introduce VESPA ($\textbf{VE}$rifiable $\textbf{S}$ymbolic $\textbf{P}$olicy $\textbf{A}$daptation), a framework for targeted fine-tuning of decision tree policies. We show that using counterexamples for policy adaptation can make existing unsafe policies safe, or at least make considerable progress towards safety. Targeted fine-tuning of the existing policy on those counterexamples enables it to learn how to avoid violating safety constraints. We thus use the result of a formal verification as a training signal for fine-tuning. On CartPole, VESPA raises the mean number of verified safe steps from 63.8 to at least 92.7, reaching after two iterations what the same loop without counterexamples reaches after ten. On MountainCarContinuous, VESPA turns an unsafe policy into a safe policy in 53 of 60 runs. We conclude that counterexamples from a verifier are an effective training signal, which can be utilized to systematically improve the safety of policies. Our implementation is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/VESPA-Submission/
tldr: VESPA is a framework that uses counterexamples from formal verification as training signals to fine-tune decision tree policies for safe reinforcement learning, improving verified safety in CartPole and MountainCarContinuous.
tldr_zh: VESPA是一个利用形式验证反例作为训练信号来微调决策树策略的框架，旨在提升强化学习中的策略安全性，在CartPole和MountainCarContinuous任务中验证了有效性。

title: Learning Martial Arts Motion Skills for Animating Opponents in VR Sparring Games
summary: Animating virtual opponents is an important yet challenging task in game development. In martial arts games, opponent motions must not only be physically plausible but also exhibit appropriate technique, timing, transitions, and target-directed intent. Traditional game animations often rely on handcrafted clips, state machine transitions, and procedural adjustments, which can be labor-intensive and may limit the behavioral diversity of non-player characters. This paper presents a martial arts motion skills learning framework for character animation in virtual sparring games. Inspired by Tang Soo Do, we collected a martial arts motion capture dataset containing isolated attacking and defending techniques, technique combinations and transitions, and contextual sparring variations. We first pretrained a reusable repertoire of martial arts motion skills from the captured data using reinforcement learning (RL) with adversarial style rewards, and then adapted these skills with task-specific rewards for target-directed striking and threat-aware evasion. We evaluated the motions generated by the learned policy through a user study, in which participants assessed their physical plausibility, smoothness, and martial arts form. To demonstrate their applicability to interactive gameplay, we developed a VR sparring prototype for Meta Quest headsets. The prototype combines policy-generated motion clips with lightweight state-based control to support interactive opponent behavior. Together, these findings support the feasibility of using a learned martial arts skill repertoire as a motion foundation for animating opponents in VR sparring games.
tldr: This paper proposes a reinforcement learning framework for learning a reusable repertoire of martial arts motion skills from motion capture data, and demonstrates its application to animating interactive opponents in a VR sparring game prototype.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种从动作捕捉数据中学习可重用武术动作技能库的强化学习框架，并将其应用于VR对战游戏中交互式对手的动画生成。

title: LightSEAD: Lightweight SE(3)-Aware Keypoint Detector through Selective Knowledge Distillation
summary: The pursuit of improved performance in deep learning has often been accompanied by increasing architectural complexity and computational demands. We explore an alternative direction: achieving more with less through structured supervision. We introduce LightSEAD, a lightweight SE(3)-aware keypoint detector initialised with calibrated Harris pseudo-labels and enriched through viewpoint-aware and appearance-aware supervision and selective knowledge distillation. LightSEAD comprises only six convolutional layers and 84,289 learnable parameters, achieving competitive repeatability across HPatches, KITTI 06 and 4Seasons while demonstrating its downstream applicability to relative pose estimation on MegaDepth-1500. Further optimised for mixed-precision inference, LightSEAD Coarse achieves approximately 909 FPS on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 and 139 FPS on a Jetson Orin Nano Super.
tldr: LightSEAD is a lightweight SE(3)-aware keypoint detector with only six convolutional layers and 84K parameters, achieving competitive repeatability and efficient relative pose estimation through calibrated Harris pseudo-labels and selective knowledge distillation.
tldr_zh: LightSEAD 是一种轻量级 SE(3) 感知关键点检测器，仅含六层卷积和 84K 参数，通过校准的 Harris 伪标签和选择性知识蒸馏，在重复性和相对位姿估计上达到有竞争力的性能。

title: EyeDiT: Anatomy-Grounded Multi-Modal Eye Generation and Simulation
summary: Synthetic eye data are critical for rapid development of eye tracking (ET) in AR/VR applications. However, existing synthetic eye generators are largely image-centric and lack a high-quality underlying 3D anatomy of the eye, which limits their control mainly to the gaze and provides no anatomical labels. To address this problem, we propose EyeDiT, an anatomy-grounded, multi-modal 3D eye generation and simulation model trained with optical coherence tomography (OCT), labeled anatomy point clouds and near-eye images. Our pipeline first trains a Multi-Modal Anatomy Variational Autoencoder (VAE), which encodes an anatomy-aware latent representation from all input modalities. Then, our Eye Latent DiT is trained to generate latent samples conditioned on the optical axis, the pupil position and radius, and the subject identity. Together with Gaussian decoders for novel-view simulation, our model enables control over the pupil, subject identity and viewpoint for data synthesis. We show that our model outperforms previous eye image synthesis models in novel-view synthesis (24.9 against 21.8 dB PSNR from a single view), and that a public ET neural network trained on our synthetic data shows a smaller sim-to-real gap than when trained on data from other generators (3.5$^\circ$ vs. 8.4$^\circ$ gaze error), approaches a network trained on real data, and further improves ET performance when combined with real data (2.3$^\circ$ vs. 2.6$^\circ$). More information is available on the project page: https://lyhan12.github.io/eyedit
tldr: EyeDiT is an anatomy-grounded multi-modal 3D eye generation and simulation model that uses OCT, labeled anatomy point clouds, and near-eye images to generate synthetic eye data with control over pupil, identity, and viewpoint, significantly improving simulated-to-real gaze estimation performance.
tldr_zh: EyeDiT是一种基于解剖学、多模态的3D眼睛生成与模拟模型，利用OCT、标注解剖点云和近眼图像生成合成眼睛数据，并控制瞳孔、身份和视角，显著提高了模拟到真实的视线估计性能。

title: Dual-Actuation Emulation of Scaled Relative Orbital Dynamics on a Free-Flyer
summary: Ground-based free-flyer testbeds reproduce the planar motion of a free-floating spacecraft using air bearings, but not the relative dynamics of spacecraft in orbit. We present a dual-actuation architecture that physically emulates Clohessy-Wiltshire dynamics on an open-source free-flyer. Two model predictive controllers run in parallel: one drives the solenoid thrusters with an orbital dynamics model, representing the spacecraft under test; the other drives bidirectional propellers that physically apply the orbital accelerations, continuously updating its reference to account for thruster-induced velocity changes. A dynamic similitude maps the orbital scenario onto the limited floor area and actuation rates of the testbed, letting the spacecraft controller run directly at orbital scale. We validate the architecture on hardware and against a high-fidelity orbital simulation, where the orbital accelerations instead arise naturally, both driven by the identical spacecraft controller. Their agreement indicates that the testbed reproduces the relative orbital motion the controller would encounter in flight.
tldr: This paper presents a dual-actuation architecture for a free-flyer testbed that physically emulates Clohessy-Wiltshire relative orbital dynamics, validated against high-fidelity simulation.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种双驱动架构，用于在自由飞行器实验台上物理模拟Clohessy-Wiltshire相对轨道动力学，并与高保真仿真进行了验证。

title: Object Pose: The Link between Weak Perspective, Paraperspective, and Full Perspective
summary: Recently, DeMenthon and Davis [4,5] proposed a method for determining the pose of a 3-D object with respect to a camera from 3-D to 2-D point correspondences. The method consists of iteratively improving the pose computed with a weak perspective camera model to converge, at the limit, to a pose estimation computed with a perspective camera model. In this paper we give an algebraic derivation of DeMenthon and Davis' method and we show that it belongs to a larger class of methods where the perspective camera model is approximated either at zero order (weak perspective) or first order (paraperspective). We describe in detail an iterative paraperspective pose computation method for both non coplanar and coplanar object points. We analyse the convergence of these methods and we conclude that the iterative paraperspective method (proposed in this paper) has better convergence properties than the iterative weak perspective method. We introduce a simple way of taking into account the orthogonality constraint associated with the rotation matrix. We analyse the sensitivity to camera calibration errors and we define the optimal experimental setup with respect to imprecise camera calibration. We compare the results obtained with this method and with a non-linear optimization method.
tldr: This paper provides an algebraic derivation of DeMenthon and Davis' iterative pose estimation method, showing it belongs to a broader family of approximations to perspective projection, and introduces an iterative paraperspective pose computation method with better convergence properties and sensitivity analysis to camera calibration errors.
tldr_zh: 本文对DeMenthon和Davis的迭代位姿估计方法进行了代数推导，表明其属于透视投影近似方法的更广泛类别，并提出了一种具有更好收敛性和相机标定误差敏感性分析的迭代平行透视位姿计算方法。

title: Modelling the human-exoskeleton interaction interface - Benchmarking MuJoCo's deformable model
summary: The human-exoskeleton interaction interface, consisting of the exoskeleton attachment and the underlying human soft tissue, can affect the transfer of assistance. MuJoCo's \textit{flexcomp} has been previously used to model the soft tissue, but its accuracy has not been benchmarked against a finite element model. We benchmarked the \textit{flexcomp} Saint Venant-Kirchhoff (StVK) and Stable Neo-Hookean (SNH) models against COMSOL's Yeoh model in three cases: \textit{case 1}) spherical indentation, \textit{case 2}) compression, and \textit{case 3}) compression of a thigh. We compared force and strain energy as a function of indentation depth, hysteresis and computation time. MuJoCo's models capture force trends with a correlation of 0.97-0.99, but showed a stiffer response, which could be attributed to the volumetric locking of the linear finite elements. The MuJoCo models systematically underestimated hysteresis as MuJoCo's Rayleigh damping could not substitute a viscoelastic model. Moreover, MuJoCo's computational advantage was speed dependent: it was 2-2.5 times faster for spherical indentation, but COMSOL was faster for the other cases, which have more degrees of freedom and contacts. Although MuJoCo's \textit{flexcomp} offers a combination of soft-tissue modelling and multibody dynamics, the limitations regarding the stiffening and hysteresis should be addressed to be used for the analysis of the human-exoskeleton interaction interface.
tldr: This paper benchmarks MuJoCo's deformable soft-tissue models (flexcomp StVK and SNH) against COMSOL's Yeoh finite element model for human-exoskeleton interaction, finding high force-trend correlation but stiffer response, underestimated hysteresis, and mixed computational speed.
tldr_zh: 本文针对人-外骨骼交互界面，将MuJoCo的可变形软组织模型（flexcomp StVK和SNH）与COMSOL的Yeoh有限元模型进行基准比较，发现力趋势相关性高，但响应更硬、滞后低估，计算速度各有优劣。

title: Hebbian self-organization of monosynaptic reflexes in a biologically realistic multiarticular limb
summary: Spinal monosynaptic reflexes depend on patterns of connectivity between muscle spindle afferents and motoneurons that should reflect musculoskeletal dynamics. One possibility is that the details of these circuits are specified genetically, but this requires an unlikely coevolution of musculoskeletal and neural elements. Here we show how biomechanical structure can determine the connectivity of self-organized spinal circuits. Using a neuromechanical model combining a multi-joint limb, proprioceptive feedback, and Hebbian plasticity driven by motor babbling, we find that biologically realistic connectivity emerges spontaneously when babbling is neither too sparse nor too frequent. This results in strong homonymous projections, weaker heteronymous projections among functional synergists, and very weak connections among antagonists. This outcome also depends on musculoskeletal morphometry. Heteronymous synergies form when proximal muscles are strongest---the characteristic gradient of mammalian limbs--whereas excessively strong biarticular muscles lead to unphysiological antagonist coupling. The mechanisms differ: homonymous connections arise from direct sensorimotor correlation during fusimotor coactivation by beta motoneurons, while heteronymous connections depend on multi-joint dynamics that emerge only after homonymous reflexes stabilize and increasing muscle strength generates multisegmental motion. Overall, this study provides a mechanistic basis for fetal sensorimotor development and generates testable predictions about the consequences of naturally occurring and experimentally induced variations.
tldr: This paper uses a neuromechanical model with Hebbian plasticity to show that spinal monosynaptic reflex connectivity can self-organize from motor babbling, matching biological patterns and depending on musculoskeletal morphometry.
tldr_zh: 本文通过神经力学模型和Hebbian可塑性，证明脊髓单突触反射连接可从运动咿呀学语中自组织形成，并与生物模式相符，且依赖于肌肉骨骼形态。

title: HHW-Ego: DSLR-Quality Enhancement for Multi-Source Wearable Ego Imaging
summary: Wearable ego-centric images are now in high demand for scenarios ranging from daily smart glass usage to embodied intelligence. But the image quality is far behind smart phone due to the lacking paired high-quality reference images and the dedicated enhancement systems. To solve this, a customized degradation pipeline is designed to generate paired samples matching wearable camera images, boosting the upper limit of enhancement performance. Besides a two-stage enhancement framework is further built: first, tuning an efficient model on the paired dataset to enhance real wearable images; second, using hyperspectral data to refine color temperature for better quality. Moreover we present HHW-Ego, a multi-source paired dataset integrating with Hyperspectral, High-dynamic range and Wearable Ego-centric data, which includes 5,000 image groups spanning indoor/outdoor and day/night scenes. On held-out paired data, Stage-1 fine-tuning improves PSNR, SSIM, Lab distance, and LPIPS for Real-ESRGAN and PFT-SR. On real wearable images, no-reference metrics, human preference, gamut analysis, and visual comparisons characterize the effects of Stage 2.
tldr: HHW-Ego presents a customized degradation pipeline and a two-stage enhancement framework to improve the quality of multi-source wearable ego-centric images, supported by a new paired dataset with hyperspectral and HDR data.
tldr_zh: HHW-Ego 提出了一种定制化的退化流水线和两阶段增强框架，以提升多源可穿戴第一人称图像质量，并构建了一个包含高光谱和HDR数据的配对数据集。

title: PsyWorld: Profile-Conditioned World Modeling for Human Behavior Prediction
summary: Understanding how stable psychometric traits and time-varying states jointly inform behavior is an important problem in computational behavioral science. Existing personalized agents commonly condition actions directly on a static profile, leaving realized state transitions unused as an explicit source of supervision. We introduce a profile-conditioned state world model that uses observed environment--behavior state transitions to learn transition-informed representations for behavioral prediction. During training, a posterior encoder quantizes realized transitions, while a prior predicts the resulting codes from the psychometric profile and pre-transition context. The prior code and predicted next state then condition macro-level behavior and simulator-grounded execution. Thus, the world model provides structured transition supervision instead of treating personality as a direct action descriptor. We evaluate the framework in VEET, a controlled behavioral simulator with human trajectories, and in AgentSociety as a structurally different synthetic environment. A participant-disjoint split of 240 training, 25 validation, and 48 test participants evaluates generalization to unseen people. On VEET, the model reaches 0.904 Top-1 accuracy (95\% CI: [0.895, 0.913]) and 0.0033 Macro KL. Ablations associate continuous next-state modeling with most of the Top-1 gain, while discrete codes and prior alignment mainly improve Top-3 and distributional alignment. These results establish transition-informed world-model supervision as useful for subject-generalized behavior prediction, without implying causal psychological mechanisms or calibrated long-horizon state dynamics.
tldr: This paper introduces a profile-conditioned state world model that leverages environment-behavior state transitions to improve human behavior prediction in simulation, demonstrating generalization to unseen participants without causal or long-horizon claims.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一种基于画像条件的状态世界模型，利用环境-行为状态转移来改进人类行为预测，并在模拟环境中展示了未见参与者的泛化能力，但不涉及因果或长期预测。

title: Enhancing Active Learning Performance with Initial Data Selection Based on Foundation Models
summary: In active object detection, selecting the initial labeled pool is essential, especially in complex datasets with expensive labeling and low resource budget. This study presents an active learning framework designed to optimize the initial training cycle of active learning for the object detection task. Our approach diverges from traditional methods by utilizing feature-based clustering from the YOLO-World model and refining images based on objectness scores rather than relying on uncertainty sampling in the initial cycle. This approach focuses on finding samples with various features and emphasizes training in areas where the foundation model is most confident. Doing so helps the model better understand different types of objects. For subsequent cycles, we employ a consistency-based sampling technique to maintain the robustness of the training process. To evaluate our method, we use two complex datasets called Aquarium and NWPU VHR-10, which are well known for their diverse object sizes and challenging conditions. In the NWPU dataset, our method increases mAP50 by an average of 6.6% in image-based evaluation. Moreover, the image refinement method shows an improvement of approximately 11% in object-based evaluation. The results show improvements in model performance and labeling time, demonstrating the advantages of using foundation models in early cycles of active learning. An implementation of the algorithm is available at https://github.com/Mhrshd-fllh/ALBoost-FM
tldr: This paper proposes an active learning framework for object detection that uses foundation model-based feature clustering and objectness refinement to select an initial labeled pool, improving performance in subsequent active learning cycles.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种用于目标检测的主动学习框架，利用基于基础模型的特征聚类和对象性细化选择初始标注池，改善了后续主动学习循环的性能。

title: 3D GameDev Arena: Benchmarking Coding Agents That Plan, Build, and Playtest extreme Long-Horizon Browser Games
summary: Coding agents now resolve repository issues and generate compact playable games, but whether they can build a large 3D game from scratch remains open. Such games tightly couple mechanics, scenes, assets, and interaction logic, and their quality rests on player enjoyment, which existing benchmarks rarely assess. Thus, we introduce 3D GameDev Arena, a first extreme long-horizon benchmark of 108 from-scratch game-development tasks across 14 genres. Given only a text specification and UI/UX reference images, a fully automated plan--implement--test--repair pipeline builds each task into a self-contained browser game. Runs average $\sim$1,000 LLM calls ; the longest uses 14,407 calls, 2.13B tokens, and 608 assets. Evaluation spans (1) objective code-level functional acceptance against the game specification, (2) agent-based QA and playtesting of 3D presentation and playability, and (3) blind pairwise Bradley-Terry human preference in a public arena. The preliminary findings indicate that long-horizon 3D game development remains far from solved, and code-level correctness alone does not dictate player preference. The public arena is hosted online.

title: 4D-TEMPO: Differentiable 4D-STEM ptychography via fast Physics Optimizers
summary: Electron ptychography recovers atomic structure from 4D-STEM data: diffraction patterns at multiple positions of a scanned probe. Current codes reconstruct an image and read atoms off it, or fit atoms under an $L_1$ loss; neither gives per-atom uncertainty. We propose 4D-TEMPO, a differentiable physical renderer that fits the atoms, the microscope, and the detector directly to the recorded electron counts under a Poisson likelihood. The output is a list of atoms, each a Gaussian primitive with a 3D position, a thermal width, and a model-conditional error bar from the Fisher information. The Fisher information also conditions the solver, gives the dose (electrons per Å$^2$) each parameter needs, and separates calibration from imaging. On a simulated WSe$_2$ bilayer, starting from the published reconstruction, fitted atoms cut in-plane error by a third (3.2 vs. 4.8 pm) and depth error by 40-61% against its 3D peaks. Depth comes from multiple scattering into the dark field, the faint counts outside the direct beam. The two layers, $10\times$ closer than the depth of field, separate; per-atom depth then follows the layer geometry. When the model is well specified, the bars are calibrated (69% of position coordinates within $1σ$). On experimental WSe$_2$, fitted atoms predict held-out patterns better than the three published codes we test. With free probe modes where atoms are incomplete, the same likelihood predicts best on all three held-out benchmarks, matches every WSe$_2$ baseline in 5 min against up to 20.5 h, and passes torchslice at its released setting 180$\times$ sooner on PrScO$_3$. Per-atom error bars, planned doses, and fast reconstruction point to low-dose, real-time 3D imaging of beam-sensitive and dynamic materials.

title: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises
summary: Agentic AI platforms-systems in which LLM agents plan, invoke tools, retain memory and coordinate to change the state of enterprise systems-are being procured faster than they can be measured. Public agent benchmarks score models in fixed harnesses; enterprises buy integrated platforms whose orchestration, memory, governance and tooling layers dominate outcomes, and they buy them largely on the strength of vendor demonstrations. We report an industrial evaluation programme ("bakeoff") run by the innovation laboratory of a global bank in which ten platforms-spanning open-source frameworks, proprietary products and hyperscaler ecosystems-were assessed by a cross-functional panel on nine capability dimensions across three financial-services workloads: counterparty credit risk, retrieval-augmented generation and process automation. Scores separate the field into three tiers that are stable under alternative weightings, and surface workload-specific strengths that aggregates hide. A secondary analysis, however, finds Cronbach's alpha = 0.98 across nominally distinct dimensions and rank correlations >= 0.93 with the total for eight of nine: a halo effect indicating that demonstration-based scoring measures presentation as much as capability. From these lessons we propose a gate-then-score evaluation protocol with four layers (capability, execution reliability, governance gates, business value), trace-level reliability metrics estimated over repeated runs, an autonomy-readiness scale and a reproducibility protocol. We state precisely what the present evidence supports, and what a controlled harness must add to turn enterprise platform evaluation from structured judgement into measurement.

title: A Fast, Programmable GPU-to-CPU Invocation Layer for GPU-Initiated Communication
summary:
Modern GPU workloads increasingly rely on device-initiated communication to let GPU kernels communicate directly without synchronizing with the host at kernel boundaries. Existing libraries commonly favor placing transport control on GPU threads, an approach known as GPUDirect Async (GDA), and treat reverse offload to host proxy threads as a slower fallback. We argue that reverse offload can outperform GDA and should be a first-class communication path. We further propose exposing reverse offload as a programming interface that lets users define workload-specific communication operations.
  We present KIWI, a programmable reverse-offload framework that achieves sub-microsecond one-way device-to-host latency and hundreds of millions of operations per second. We address practical challenges of scaling reverse offload, including contention on shared queues, polling overhead, and load imbalance across proxies. KIWI-P2P, a SHMEM-like library built on KIWI, outperforms state-of-the-art GDA implementations in both latency and bandwidth. More importantly, KIWI-EP redesigns low-latency mixture-of-experts dispatch and combine kernels around workload-defined operations, lowering expert-parallel communication latency by up to 2.3x over the best existing backend on AMD GPUs and time per output token in vLLM by up to 29%. The source code of KIWI is available at https://github.com/AMDResearch/kiwi.

title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics. The training and evaluation data span 36 behavioural domains and 78 social science experiments, comprising 288,307 person records, 1,411,750 atomic behavioural decisions, and 99,953 psychometric assessments over 109 psychological constructs. In our evaluations, Chiron's psychological measurements agree more closely with human self-reports and exhibit fewer biases that undermine psychometric validity. It predicts individual behaviour more accurately than frontier LLMs (up to 28.4% relative improvement). In simulations of social science experiments, it more accurately captures the direction and magnitude of human experimental effects (82.2--94.3% lower effect-size estimation error). Together, these results establish Chiron as a unified computational instrument for measuring and predicting human behaviour.

title: A Free Lunch: Gradient Averaging Achieves Optimal Statistical Efficiency in Newton Sketch
summary: We study statistical inference for online sketched Newton methods, in which each Newton system is approximately solved by an inner randomized sketching solver. Existing work reveals a computational--statistical trade-off: the sketching solver (and its accelerated variants) reduces the per-step cost of Newton methods from $O(d^3)$ to $O(d^2)$, but the randomness introduced by sketching also inflates the limiting covariance of both the last and the averaged Newton iterates. In this work, we address this trade-off via gradient averaging. We show that simply replacing the stochastic gradient with a moving average at each step can mitigate, and in some cases eliminate, the trade-off in Newton sketch. Importantly, gradient averaging requires no additional oracle evaluations and leaves the contraction bound of the inner sketching solver unchanged. In particular, we prove that the last sketched Newton iterate with gradient averaging attains a limiting covariance no larger than that without gradient averaging, while the averaged iterate even attains the minimax optimal limiting covariance, matching that of the exact Newton method. To our knowledge, this is the first analysis showing that randomness introduced to improve computational efficiency need not compromise statistical efficiency as long as proper gradient estimates are used. The key analytical challenge is that gradient averaging destroys the crucial martingale difference structure underlying central limit theorem arguments. We overcome this challenge by analyzing the coupled two-timescale recursions governing the iterate and the gradient estimator. Numerical experiments on linear and logistic regression support our theoretical covariance comparisons.

title: A Hardware-Aware Comprehensive Study of Edge Vision Deployment with A Unified Hardware-Model-Runtime Mapping Framework
summary: The rapid growth of deep learning has driven the deployment of computer vision directly on resource-constrained edge devices. However, the extreme heterogeneity of edge hardware architectures poses major challenges in selecting and designing suitable vision models. This survey bridges the gap between edge hardware constraints, model architectures, and deployment software toolchains. We establish a comprehensive taxonomy classifying edge hardware into three distinct tiers: mid-range devices (GPUs and dedicated NPUs or TPUs), dedicated embedded MPU or SoC processors, and microcontrollers (MCUs). We aggregate and analyze multi-source benchmark results for image classification and object detection across the computing spectrum, spanning from tens of watts down to milliwatt-scale bare-metal MCUs. Based on these empirical findings, we propose a two-tiered hardware-to-model mapping framework that provides concrete model selection matrices across performance priorities (Speed, Balanced, Accuracy) and actionable architectural design principles (peak SRAM budgeting, resolution-first scaling, and algorithm-compiler co-design). Finally, we highlight critical deployment challenges including toolchain fragmentation, operator incompatibility, and Vision Transformer feasibility, and outline promising future research directions in on-device adaptation and sustainable Edge AI.

title: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning and Out-of-Context Hallucination
summary: Large language models can infer and follow specific rules through in-context learning (ICL), yet may fail to remain faithful to provided evidence, giving rise to out-of-context (OOC) hallucination. Existing work has largely investigated the underlying mechanisms of ICL and OOC hallucination along separate lines. However, this separation obscures the mechanistic basis for these seemingly opposing outcomes. In this work, we study this contrast through the unified view of functional roles in dynamic context. The key observation is that role information can be internally represented without reliably constraining output. We derive a first-order decomposition to characterize the role effect, showing that its substantial influence depends on two necessary conditions, namely sufficient contribution magnitude and coherent signed aggregation. Causal analysis further shows that role span contributions affect key token choices involving response structure, content selection, and factual values. We further show that role-consistent choices depend on sufficient role span support at these key decisions, while failing choices can be reversed when this support overcomes the deficit. These findings support a common mechanistic view of ICL and OOC hallucination: each functional role defines the pattern of output decisions over which role span contributions must remain effective, and differences in this organization account for the seemingly opposing outcomes.

title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models
summary: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes. We formalize diverse generation as sampling a size-$K$ subset of complete strings from a determinantal point process (DPP), where the likelihood encodes item quality, and the embedding geometry encodes repulsion between similar outputs. Exact inference over all strings is intractable, so we propose PoolDPP: draw a finite candidate pool from a tractable proposal, importance-weight the candidates toward the target quality, and run a $K$-DPP sampler on the induced pool kernel; a greedy MAP variant provides deterministic selection. We prove a finite-sample bound with an explicit constant: the KL divergence between the sampler's output and the target $K$-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size. Empirically, PoolDPP extends the quality--diversity frontier on open-ended generation and the precision--recall frontier on ambiguous text-to-SQL (Ambrosia), and on mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), it raises diversity at about the same pass@$K$.

title: A Rank-One Bypass of Fixed Linear Erasure
summary: Linear concept erasure can make a target unreadable to a specified family of linear classifiers applied to a model's current internal features. In an open-weight release, however, an attacker can modify the layers that produce those features. We study a fixed affine erasure layer whose upstream model is allowed to change. If the layer transmits even one direction visible to an allowed downstream classifier, the attacker can write a target score into that direction and carry it through the layer. We show that this condition is also necessary, and that for a nonconstant linear target score the required change is a rank-one affine update. Across six CIFAR-10 class-pair tasks, the route restores nearly all pre-erasure target performance and can leave a deployed benign linear head's scores unchanged to numerical tolerance. We then price the attack: with eight target labels and 2,000 unlabelled calibration examples, a 10% mean relative feature edit yields 79.8% test accuracy, which is 91.2% of the fitted score's gain over chance; tighter edit limits sharply reduce success. Linear guardedness therefore remains a valid guarantee about the current representation, but it is not by itself a tamper-resistance guarantee for an editable open-weight model.

title: A System 1 Decision Model for Medical Multiple-Choice Questions Built on Frozen Language Models
summary: A System 1 model answers a multiple-choice question in a single pass. A frozen language model turns the question and each option into vectors, two small, trained heads place them in a shared space, and the closest option wins. The design has been shown on agent decisions, but we are not aware of a study of how far it goes on exam questions that need medical knowledge, where the right option is often no more similar to the question than the wrong ones. We rebuilt the recipe from scratch for MedMCQA and trained only two projection heads and one temperature on top of frozen Qwen3.5-0.8B, Granite-4.2-3B and Qwen3-8B, using a contrastive loss with in-batch and hard negatives and a mask for repeated answers. With plain last-token vectors, both small encoders answer about one question in three correctly (33.1% and 33.0% on 3,842 held-out questions, where chance is 25.0%). Writing each text inside a one-word-summary prompt and lowering the learning rate of the heads raised this to 41.7% and 42.5% for the two small encoders and to 46.0% +-0.2 (three seeds) for Qwen3-8B. Shuffling the questions against the options returns accuracy to chance, so the heads do use the question. Flan-PaLM and Med-PaLM 2 report 57.6% and 72.3% on MedMCQA under a different protocol, so ours is a cheap, fast baseline and not a competitive system. We also say what our evidence cannot show: validation gains were about 1.7 to 2 times the test gains, and we could not separate the effect of reading several encoder layers from the other changes.

title: A Systematic Analysis of a Small Optimal Subspace for Physics-Informed Neural Networks: $n$-DAS $\subset \mathbb{R}^p$
summary: The search for a low-dimensional subspace that governs neural network training has been a persistent goal in optimization. Yet subspaces defined by Hessian eigenvalue magnitude, such as the dominant/bulk decomposition underlying Dom-SGD and Bulk-SGD, have repeatedly failed to capture where optimization takes place, and adaptive Krylov-based alternatives built on energy-fraction thresholds show promise but still struggle at lower eigenmodes. We argue this failure is structural: the directions of highest curvature are not, in general, the directions along which training moves. We introduce the dominant aligned subspace (DAS), constructed from a full eigendecomposition of the Hessian but selected by gradient alignment rather than eigenvalue magnitude, as a tool for understanding optimization dynamics and a foundation for designing methods that exploit them. To expose this structure under the hardest conditions, we use physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) as a testbed: differential operators from the parabolic, elliptic, and hyperbolic classes induce severely ill-conditioned, anisotropic loss landscapes. Across Poisson, heat, wave, and viscous Burgers benchmarks DAS-restricted training with a line search matches full-space training even where the projected Hessian remains ill-conditioned, showing empirically that convergence does not require all Hessian eigendirections but only a low-dimensional, gradient-aligned subset. We extend the analysis to Gauss-Newton within the DAS and discuss what this structure implies for future subspace-aware optimizers.

title: A$^3$Bench: Compositional Reasoning over Aggressive Interactions in Videos
summary: Recent Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved strong performance on general video understanding benchmarks, yet their ability to reason about participant roles in aggressive interactions remains largely unexplored. Existing violence and crime datasets primarily evaluate whether aggression occurs, without testing whether models can identify who performed the action, who received it, and how participants are related within the scene. To address this gap, we introduce A$^3$Bench, a benchmark to study aggressive action and association in videos. The benchmark evaluates whether models can jointly recognize aggressive actions, distinguish aggressors from victims and bystanders, and correctly bind actions to participants under challenging distractor settings. We benchmark 17 multimodal models and find that they struggle substantially on fine-grained aggressive-scene understanding. Performance degrades consistently as reasoning complexity increases, with models frequently confusing aggressors with victims or bystanders, revealing a systematic failure in role-action association rather than coarse aggression recognition alone. We further observe that increasing model scale or generic reasoning models experience limited improvement. Finally, we explore a simple role-graph prompting strategy that encourages structured reasoning over participant interactions, leading to improvements in compositional reasoning. Our findings highlight that reliable aggressive-scene understanding remains a major challenge for current MLLMs and motivate future research on role-aware video reasoning beyond coarse violence detection. Code and dataset: https://github.com/austincbaker/A3Bench.

title: ABSClaw: From Invented Worlds to Reality-Grounded Social Simulation
summary: LLM-based artificial societies exhibit rich behavior but often lack scientific grounding: personas and environments are assumed, interaction networks are synthetic, and simulators are generated as free-form code, making results difficult to tie to real populations and sensitive to the backbone model. We argue that simulated worlds should be sampled from observed data, while simulation logic should be implemented by composing operations from a shared, task-independent vocabulary. In this paper, we introduce ABSClaw, a zero-code agent that compiles natural-language requests into executable, reality-grounded social simulations. ABSClaw grounds who acts, where they act, and with whom they interact in survey and census data, geospatial sources, and real networks. It expresses state transitions through 26 atomic operations. To support an open and extensible ecosystem, ABSClaw further allows capabilities to be added as lifecycle-scoped skills without modifying its core. Furthermore, we propose ABSBench, a benchmark of 193 real-world social-simulation tasks. On ABSBench, ABSClaw achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated social simulators. Three real-world case studies show that grounding personas, environments, and interaction networks each improves agreement with observed outcomes. With one runtime skill, ABSClaw executes 13 population-scale simulations, collectively involving 25 million agents. Together, these results demonstrate ABSClaw's real-world fidelity, extensibility, and scalability.

title: ACUS: An Angular Calibrated Uncertainty Score for Incomplete-View CT
summary: Sparse-view and limited-arc computed tomography (CT) are commonly treated as projection completion: a network fills an unmeasured view, and the result is ranked by similarity to one ground-truth image. That score can be high even when the query angle is far from every acquired measurement, because a learned prior may invent anatomy the scan never constrained. Existing protocols therefore leave a basic question unanswered: how does predictive reliability change with distance from the acquired views? We propose the Angular Calibrated Uncertainty Score (ACUS) to answer that question. ACUS is the Winkler interval score of a nominal 90% predictive interval on held-out projections, binned by distance to the nearest acquired view. It charges interval width and adds a large miss penalty when a held-out pixel falls outside the interval, so a narrow band helps only when coverage holds. We use collapse on acquired angles as a necessary consistency check on the predictor. On chest and dental cone-beam orbits, interval width grows with the angular gap. Empirical coverage ranges from 77% to 92%, and the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of the point estimate falls as the width rises. Nearest-neighbor, interpolation, and point completion, each given one residual scale, have zero reported far coverage and incur outside-distance penalties. ACUS exposes gap-dependent overconfidence that a point-estimate PSNR alone does not measure.

title: AG-BFGS: Foundations for Accelerated Geometry Learning
summary: We introduce an accelerated geometry-learning framework for BFGS that incorporates momentum into the learning of Hessian inverse approximations. We prove that the resulting accelerated updates satisfy explicit stability conditions and preserve positive definiteness within admissible parameter regions. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over the corresponding non-accelerated schemes while maintaining numerical stability. These results provide the first rigorous theoretical foundation for accelerated quasi-Newton learning and bridge the gap between empirical observations and mathematical guarantees for accelerated second-order methods.

title: AGAMOTTO: An AI-Enabled Framework for Time-Critical Tactical Course-of-Action Evaluation and Generation
summary: Current command and control (C2) platforms lack integrated simulation capabilities that would allow commanders to dynamically explore courses of action (COAs) during live operations. This paper presents ongoing research and contributions to the development of AGAMOTTO (Advanced Guidance and Analytics for Military Operations, Tactical Threats, and Outcomes) as part of the overarching NGC2 program, which advances the Army's efforts to modernize C2 systems, such as the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK). The paper outlines the current design, preliminary findings, and the remaining research tasks, with an emphasis on how the completed work will support tactical decision-making in future time-constrained environments. While the full system is still under development, initial development and results demonstrate the feasibility of AGAMOTTO. Early experiments highlight both the potential benefits and practical constraints of deploying AI-enabled tools in operational settings, and introduce lessons learned and a viable training strategy to make AI-generated COAs feasible in tactical scenarios.

title: APS: Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection for Long Video Understanding
summary: Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) have significantly improved video understanding capabilities, yet processing long videos remains challenging due to the substantial computational cost of extensive visual inputs. Frame selection offers an efficient alternative, but many existing region-based methods rely on fixed or predefined temporal partitions, which may result in suboptimal temporal regions, compromising subsequent budget allocation and frame selection. In this work, we propose Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection (APS), a training-free framework that adapts temporal partitions to local variations in query-frame relevance. Specifically, APS formulates temporal partitioning as a complexity-regularized fitting problem, jointly optimizing partition boundaries and local models through dynamic programming. The resulting adaptive temporal partitions guide frame budget allocation based on query relevance and temporal extent, enabling informative frame selection under limited visual budgets. Extensive experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate that APS consistently improves performance across diverse LVLM backbones, achieving the highest average gains over uniform sampling among competing methods. Further analyses validate the effectiveness of adaptive partitioning and demonstrate its generalizability across model scales, similarity encoders, and advanced LVLMs.

title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
summary: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. ARISE uses the model itself or a teacher model to attribute the failures and propose corrections. Then, ARISE keeps the corrections as retrievable micro memory, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts a rule update only if held-out accuracy rises. Across 14 enterprise-workflow domains from SOP-Bench and $τ^2$-bench using 5 models, ARISE-Teacher, which uses Claude Opus 4.6 for attribution and consolidation, gains 10.9 pp over the baseline on SOP-Bench and 5.8 pp on $τ^2$-bench. ARISE-Teacher also outperforms GEPA by 4.5 pp on $τ^2$-bench and 1.4 pp on SOP-Bench. With the deployment model as its own attributor, ARISE-Self still gains 10.0 pp on SOP-Bench. ARISE-Teacher uses 4.0% fewer model calls and 5.2% fewer output tokens at comparable per-task cost (-1.0%).

title: ART: Bridging the Embodiment Gap in 3D Human-to-Robot Affordance Transfer
summary: 3D affordance acts as a critical link between perception and action, providing priors for robotic manipulation. While existing approaches predominantly leverage human priors as direct references, they often overlook that affordance is not an object-intrinsic property but is inherently coupled with the agent's embodiment. Due to the structural and morphological disparities between human hands and robot end-effectors, directly applying human priors causes severe incompatibility for robotic execution. Motivated by this, we introduce a novel task setting, 3D Human-to-Robot Affordance Transfer, which addresses the affordance misalignment arising from distinct embodiment structures. To support this task, we construct the Human-Robot Paired Affordance Dataset (HPAD), the first large-scale 3D affordance benchmark in which every object is annotated with both human-prior and simulation-validated robot labels. HPAD covers 2,137 objects across 80 categories and 13 atomic action primitives, yielding over 27,000 object-action pairs. On top of HPAD, we propose the 3D Affordance tRansfer neTwork (ART). ART first filters geometric false positives in the human prior via a reliability gating stream, then reconstructs the prior into a robot-actionable distribution through hierarchical reconstruction and a graph-diffusion refinement that resolves the topological mismatch between human and robot affordances. Experiments on HPAD demonstrate the reliability of the proposed task and the superiority of ART. We further validate ART on a 6-DoF arm with a parallel-jaw gripper in a 2,400-execution benchmark across 12 objects and 4 action categories; ART attains the best success rate (86.5% over its 480 trials), confirming the practicality of the transfer paradigm. Project page: https://derek0907.github.io/ART/

title: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination
summary: Vision-Language Models increasingly rely on textual reasoning to solve advanced multimodal tasks. Despite its effectiveness, this paradigm faces two fundamental limitations. First, relying on textual reasoning alone can limit perceptual ability in vision-centric questions, where accurate answers depend on interpreting task-relevant visual evidence. Second, applying textual reasoning uniformly across inputs overlooks question-dependent variation in both reasoning modality and depth, often producing verbose and unnecessary traces when little logical inference is required. To this end, we propose Adaptive Visual-Textual Reasoning (AVTR), which introduces visual imagination as a complementary reasoning modality to textual thinking, enabling the model to revisit its visual observations and distill the salient evidence through generative visual reflection. Furthermore, we formulate reasoning-modality selection as a learned routing problem, allowing a single policy to adaptively harness the complementary strengths of visual reflection and textual reasoning in response to the perceptual and inferential demands of the input. Across 16 benchmarks, AVTR improves the average score by 4.5 points over Qwen3.5 baseline, while reducing inference latency by 33\%. It also scales effectively into a smaller size backbone, outperforming the evaluated 2B-scale baselines.

title: Accelerating Distributed Digital Ising Machines
summary: Ising machines, dedicated accelerators built around the dynamics of Ising-like spin models, have emerged as a leading platform for combinatorial optimization and probabilistic sampling. The problems that motivate them require millions of spins, far beyond the on-chip capacity of any single device, so a practical Ising machine must distribute its computation across many devices. Prior work reports throughput at a single operating point, leaving the binding resource unidentified and platform crossovers measurable only by experiment; no calibrated cross-platform cost model of distributed Ising machines has been reported, nor have systematic techniques to accelerate their Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) workloads. This work presents a calibrated cost model that decomposes digital Ising sweep time into compute, memory, synchronization, and inter-device communication terms, validated with 4.8% mean error across three GPU generations, FPGA and ASIC up to 1 million spins. Guided by the model, we address each term in turn and propose: (i) a data placement strategy, worth up to 4.2$\times$ speedup; (ii) multi-rate and bounded-staleness schedules that relax the barrier that Gibbs sampling imposes, cutting time-to-solution (TTS) by up to 3.16$\times$ on three benchmarks; and (iii) a phase-offset streaming dataflow that hides boundary exchange behind interior computation whenever a link satisfies a latency-transparency criterion, yielding up to 1.25$\times$/1.74$\times$/2.01$\times$ on an H200 pair, a ZCU106 pair, and a four-board XEM8320 $2{\times}2$ mesh. The streaming dataflow is also implemented on a fabricated four-chip 28 nm ASIC sustaining 28.1 Gflips/s at 4.81 pJ/flip.

title: AdaS-ViT: Test-Time Adaptive Routing for Spiking Vision Transformers with Ultra-High Energy Efficiency
summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise event-driven and energy-efficient vision, yet existing spiking vision transformers (S-ViTs) largely confine spiking tokens to fixed and uniform firing schemes along the temporal, spatial and channel dimensions, whereas suppressing the computational redundancy thus incurred calls for adaptive firing mechanisms that operate jointly across all three axes at test time. To this end, we propose the Adaptive Efficient Integrate-and-Fire (AdaE-IF) model, which consults the attention score of each spiking token and routes salient regions to fine-grained firing patterns while assigning energy-frugal coarse patterns to the remaining regions. Building on AdaE-IF, we further introduce Spiking Gated Self-Attention (S-GSA) and Spiking Local-Gated Unit (S-LGU), which enforce selective spike emission at token and channel granularity. We integrate the aforementioned mechanisms and modules into AdaS-ViT, a test-time adaptive-routing architecture trained with a progressive spatio-temporal curriculum that stabilizes the co-adaptation of firing precision and routing masks. Extensive experiments across benchmarks spanning diverse data scales and modalities demonstrate that AdaS-ViT consistently achieves highly competitive performance. Notably, on ImageNet-1k it consumes only 1.02 to 2.45 millijoules per image and attains an accuracy-per-energy ratio of 32$\times$ to 72$\times$, operating in an economical inference regime and thereby pushing the energy-efficiency boundary further.

title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
summary: AI agents increasingly collaborate across organizational boundaries, invoking tools and interacting with agents operated by independent entities.
